summary: Prospect Mountain, Lake George: 35 ft wooden lookout (1910), 47 ft steel Aermotor tower (1932), closed after 1970 season and removed; summit road since 1969.

facts.design: 35 ft wooden lookout tower (1910); later 47 ft Aermotor LS40 steel tower with observer cabin (1932)
facts.status_note: Closed at the end of the 1970 fire lookout season and later removed; no remains described in sources.

access.note: Summit reached by the road built in 1969 that lets visitors drive to the top. No tower remains are described in sources.

visit.trail_note: Alternative hiking path follows the route of the old cable railroad (Warren County Historian).

facts.agency: Forest, Fish and Game Commission (1910); Conservation Department (1932)

events.note: Forest, Fish and Game Commission set up a 35 ft wooden lookout tower at a cost of $107.16
Hotel at the summit was the headquarters for the observer after repairs and a new roof
Observer Adelbert Brown used the summit hotel as his shelter; its cupola was his lookout station
State report calls the new tower a replacement for an older building whose top served as a lookout; the 47 ft Aermotor LS40 steel tower and observer cabin were built the same year
Wikipedia says the building at the top of the mountain burned down in 1932; the state report does not say so, see resolved_conflicts
CCC youths began setting poles for a state telephone line to the summit, linking the tower with the U.S. Army air defense command in Watertown
Road built up the mountain, allowing people to drive to the summit
Tower closed at the end of the 1970 fire lookout season because of increased use of aerial fire detection

corrections.proposed: Forest, Fish and Game Commission (1910); Conservation Department (1932)
corrections.why: The current value is the opening words of the 1910 note, not an agency. The 1910 and 1932 reports name the two agencies.
10.7 m (35 ft) is the 1910 wooden tower. The steel tower in place from 1932 until closure in 1970 was 47 ft, per the Starr list and Wikipedia.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Wikipedia says the building at the top of the mountain burned down in 1932. The 1932 state report, quoted by the Eastern US Lookouts page, describes the new tower as a replacement for a former building and does not mention a fire. The story reports both.

notes_for_editor: Two record fixes proposed (agency parse error 'July 1910:'; height 10.7 m is the 1910 tower, the 1932-1970 tower was 47 ft). The 1970 closure year rests on Wikipedia, which cites the NYS FFLA searchable list (nysffla.org/alphalist.html). That list was not read; check it before publishing. Starr's list gives no removal date. Summit elevation differs across sources (1953 article 2,200 ft; Wikipedia 2,018 ft; Starr 2,020 ft); not used in the story. The Richard Horn memoir is a personal recollection and is hedged in the story. No new photos found; photo search not run within budget. Ruins/remains today: none described in any source read.
